brewers.name: V60 01
brewers.notes: 60-degree cone with spiral ribs and one large hole; flow depends mostly on grind and pouring. 01 size is sold for 1 to 2 cups. Comes in plastic, ceramic, glass, metal and copper; material mainly changes heat retention (preheat ceramic and glass).

brewers.name: V60 02
brewers.notes: The most common V60 size, 1 to 4 cups. Same spiral ribs and single large hole as the 01. Plastic, ceramic, glass, metal and copper versions; preheat ceramic and glass well.

brewers.name: V60 03
brewers.notes: Large V60 for batches of up to about 6 cups; same geometry as the 01 and 02.

brewers.name: V60 Mugen
brewers.notes: V60 variant with a single continuous rib, designed for slower, one-pour style brewing.

brewers.name: Switch
brewers.notes: A V60 cone on a base with a valve: close it to steep like an immersion brewer, open it to drain. Lets you mix immersion and percolation in one brew.

brewers.name: 102 dripper
brewers.notes: Wedge (trapezoid) dripper with three small holes; slower, more forgiving drawdown than a V60.

brewers.name: Pour-over cone
brewers.notes: Classic wedge-shaped dripper with a small outlet; slow, forgiving and cheap. Uses Melitta #2 or #4 filters.

brewers.name: Chemex
brewers.notes: Glass carafe and cone in one. Thick bonded paper gives a very clean, light-bodied cup; usually brewed a little coarser than a V60. 3, 6, 8 and 10 cup sizes.

brewers.name: Origami Dripper
brewers.notes: Japanese porcelain cone with 20 deep folds; takes cone filters for a fast V60-like flow or Wave-style flat filters for a flat-bed brew.

brewers.name: Meimon dripper
brewers.notes: Cone with ribs only near the bottom, so the paper seals higher up; slower flow and more body than a V60.

brewers.name: Flower Dripper
brewers.notes: Cone with petal-shaped ribs that keep the paper off the wall for a quick, even drawdown. Cup1 and Cup4 sizes.

brewers.name: Deep Dripper
brewers.notes: Taller, narrower cone for a deeper coffee bed; sold in Deep 27 and Deep 45 versions.

brewers.name: Crystal Eye dripper
brewers.notes: Clear plastic V60-style cone with ribs; takes standard 01/02 cone filters.

brewers.name: Graycano Dripper
brewers.notes: German double-walled cone of ceramic-coated cast aluminium, from Leipzig. Broken V-shaped 'Lava Ribs' are meant to break up air and water channels for an even bed; holds heat well.

brewers.name: UFO Dripper
brewers.notes: Very wide, shallow ceramic cone (80-degree walls) made in South Korea from Korean clay; aims for a cone's flavour with a flat bed's consistency. Takes UFO 80-degree papers, or folded cone filters.

brewers.name: Nel drip / Woodneck
brewers.notes: Traditional Japanese cloth-filter pour-over; rich, round body. Keep the cloth wet and refrigerated between uses.

brewers.name: Wave 155
brewers.notes: Flat bed with three small holes and fluted filters; very consistent. 155 size suits roughly 1 to 2 cups.

brewers.name: Wave 185
brewers.notes: Larger Wave for 2 to 4 cups; same three-hole flat bed and fluted 185 filters.

brewers.name: April Brewer
brewers.notes: Flat-bottom brewer designed by Patrik Rolf (April Coffee, Copenhagen); he used it at the 2019 World Brewers Cup, where it earned the highest cup score in the open service round. Three ridges hold a flat-bottom (Kalita-style) filter over a conical drain hole.

brewers.name: Orea V4
brewers.notes: UK brewer with four swappable bases: Classic (flat, a little restriction), Open (focuses flow to the centre), Fast (very open, suits finer grinds; the base Martin Wölfl used to win the 2024 World Brewers Cup) and APEX (between cone and flat). Narrow (to about 28 g) and Wide (to about 36 g) versions; both take 185-size filters.

brewers.name: Stagg [X]
brewers.notes: Double-walled stainless flat-bottom dripper for single cups; holds temperature well.

brewers.name: Stagg [XF]
brewers.notes: Larger version of the Stagg [X] for bigger doses or 2 cups.

brewers.name: Tricolate
brewers.notes: Flat-bed brewer with a shower screen and no bypass, built for high extraction with a grind between pour-over and espresso. Scott Rao's recipe: 20 g coffee, 400 g water at 100 C poured as 60 g, 170 g and 170 g, 7 to 10 minutes total.

brewers.name: Pulsar
brewers.notes: No-bypass flat-bed brewer with an adjustable flow valve, designed with Jonathan Gagné. Close the valve for a full-immersion bloom or steep, open it to drain.

brewers.name: Clever Dripper
brewers.notes: Cone that steeps with a valve that opens when set on a cup. Very forgiving; most people grind a touch coarser than for a V60.

brewers.name: Immersion Dripper
brewers.notes: Porcelain cone with a lever-operated valve; steep, then release. Takes cone filters.

brewers.name: French press
brewers.notes: Full immersion with a metal mesh plunger; heavy body with some fines and oils. Coarse grind, steep about 4 minutes or longer.

brewers.name: Espro Press
brewers.notes: French press with a double micro-filter basket for a much cleaner cup; Espro also sells paper inserts for the coffee model.

brewers.name: BIRD
brewers.notes: 'Brewed In Reverse Direction': coffee and water steep together, then turning a wing nut lifts the filter pod up through the slurry and the vacuum draws the brew through the bed, with no bypass. Ships with a stainless-steel filter pod; Cafec abaca papers are an option. Grind in the pour-over range is a starting point.

brewers.name: AeroPress (original)
brewers.notes: Steep then press. Works with paper or metal discs, standard or inverted, and a very wide grind range. Accessories like a flow-control cap change how it drips.

brewers.name: AeroPress Go
brewers.notes: Travel AeroPress that packs into its own mug; slightly smaller capacity than the original.

brewers.name: AeroPress XL
brewers.notes: Double-size AeroPress for larger batches; uses its own larger filters.

brewers.name: AeroPress Clear
brewers.notes: AeroPress in a clear chamber so you can watch the brew; same filters and recipes as the original.

brewers.name: Delter Coffee Press
brewers.notes: Press brewer that steeps, then gently pushes the brew through a paper filter; often compared to the AeroPress.

brewers.name: Moka pot
brewers.notes: Stovetop brewer using steam pressure; strong, espresso-like coffee. Grind finer than filter but coarser than espresso; start with hot water and pull off the heat as it sputters.

brewers.name: Brikka
brewers.notes: Moka pot with a pressure valve that builds more pressure before release, giving a thicker, crema-like top.

brewers.name: Cezve / ibrik (Turkish)
brewers.notes: Very finely ground coffee heated with water (and often sugar) in a small pot and served unfiltered; let the grounds settle in the cup.

brewers.name: Phin filter (Vietnamese)
brewers.notes: Small metal gravity filter set on the cup; usually served with condensed milk. Nguyen Coffee Supply recommends a fine grind for its phins; too fine and it stops dripping.

brewers.name: Siphon / vacuum pot
brewers.notes: Vapour pressure pushes water up into the coffee, then a vacuum pulls the brew back down through a cloth, paper or metal filter. Clean, aromatic and hot.

brewers.name: Cold brew jar / pitcher
brewers.notes: Coarse coffee steeped in cold water for many hours, then filtered; smooth and low in acidity. Many pitchers use a fine mesh insert.

brewers.name: Toddy cold brew system
brewers.notes: Large-batch cold brew concentrate system with a felt filter.

brewers.name: Kyoto / slow-drip tower
brewers.notes: Ice water drips slowly through the coffee over hours; uses a finer grind than immersion cold brew.

brewers.name: Espresso machine
brewers.notes: Pump or lever machine pushing about 9 bar through a fine, tamped puck.

brewers.name: Flair (Neo, Classic, Pro)
brewers.notes: Manual lever espresso press; you heat water separately and pull by hand, so preheating matters a lot.

brewers.name: Flair 58
brewers.notes: Manual lever with a 58 mm portafilter and electric preheat for the brew head.

brewers.name: Robot
brewers.notes: Manual two-arm lever espresso maker with a 58 mm basket; no electricity needed.

brewers.name: Picopresso / Nanopresso
brewers.notes: Portable hand-pumped espresso makers; Picopresso has a naked portafilter-style basket for specialty use.

brewers.name: Automatic drip machine
brewers.notes: Batch brewer with a flat or cone basket; grind usually similar to or a little coarser than pour-over.

brewers.name: Drip bag (single-serve)
brewers.notes: Pre-filled paper bag that hangs on a cup; pre-ground, so only dose and water can change.

brewers.name: Melodrip
brewers.notes: Not a brewer: a hand-held dispersion screen you pour through over any dripper to cut agitation and get a cleaner cup.

brewers.name: Other brewer
brewers.notes: Anything not in the list; pick the closest method so grind suggestions still make sense.
